queries: November 2024 Bloomberg OpenAI Google Anthropic scaling models expectations Orion

sources_considered.why: Readable contemporary summary of Bloomberg's reporting; used with explicit acknowledgment that it is secondary.
Includes a direct response from Anthropic disputing deviations from scaling laws.
Returned text stopped at a subscription prompt. Excluded as an incomplete paywall preview despite its FULL TEXT label.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI's latest model, known internally as Orion, has reportedly fallen short of the company's performance expectations, particularly in handling coding tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: The report supports contemporary acknowledgment of disappointing unreleased models; its surrounding text also describes Google difficulties and an Anthropic delay. It does not identify the scaling predictions allegedly missed, and a delay is not itself a capability shortfall.

evidence_items.locator: What are tech companies saying?, quoted statement from Anthropic spokesperson

receipt.public_excerpt: we haven't seen any signs of deviations from scaling laws.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic explicitly denied seeing departures from scaling laws. This counters the breadth of the claimed acknowledgment, while leaving open whether private assessments differed.

unresolved_gaps: The available reports do not establish which scaling-derived predictions the unreleased models missed.
Reports of disappointing performance, release delays and public denials do not establish widespread acknowledgment of the same proposition.
The original Bloomberg article was unavailable in full; its accessible summary is not independent corroboration.
